title: Our Partners
desc: The project was developed in partnership between the NuLawLab and scholars at Boston College Law School and Harvard University's Berkman Klein Center for Internet & Society.

nulawlab.title: NuLawLab
nulawlab.content:
The NuLawLab is the interdisciplinary innovation laboratory at Northeastern University School of Law.

The Lab is a leader in the global legal design movement and incubates projects that advance the democratization of law.

codeforboston.title: Code for Boston
codeforboston.content:
Code for Boston addresses local social and civic challenges through creative uses of technology. Despite the name, they are not solely focused on coding!

They foster relationships between government, nonprofit, academic, for-profit companies, residents, civic technologists, analysts, designers, and many more. Code for Boston's volunteer contributors have led the technical implementation and development of this website and platform as an open source project (see our repository on GitHub).

pid.title: Partners in Democracy
pid.content: MAPLE is an initiative of Partners in Democracy - Education, a 501(c)(3) non profit organization. Partners In Democracy is building nationwide partnerships and exploring how we can drive democracy renovation efforts forward in states around the country — starting by focusing our efforts here at home in Massachusetts.

calmatters.title: CalMatters
calmatters.content:
CalMatters is a nonprofit newsroom covering California state government. Its Digital Democracy project tracks public hearings, political donations, bills and votes in the California Legislature.

In July 2026, CalMatters and MAPLE announced a partnership to share civic technology, information and expertise, including using the technology behind Digital Democracy to suggest story ideas to local media in Massachusetts.

hypha.title: Hypha Worker Co-operative
hypha.content:
Hypha Worker Co-operative is a worker-owned technology cooperative based in Toronto.

MAPLE works with Hypha under contract on research and planning for adopting the AT Protocol, the open network behind Bluesky, for MAPLE accounts and for connecting MAPLE with other platforms.
